title: From biology to imaging: Rethinking vulnerable plaques in coronary artery disease
abstract: Coronary artery disease continues to be a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide with atherosclerosis as its underlying cause. Initial pathological studies emphasized plaque rupture as the main trigger of acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Subsequent observations identified alternative substrates, such as plaque erosion and calcific nodules, while research has increasingly recognized atherosclerosis as a chronic, inflammatory and panvascular disorder.
